note: Limits for the NMEA 2000 bus checks (plan 0037). Every figure names its sources. Where sources disagree the lower figure is used. Advisory planning figures, not a copy of the standard. Review before a release (docs/bus-checks.md).

garmin-length.title: NMEA 2000 Cable Length and Device Limitations
garmin-length.says: 100 m between any two points of the network, a drop at most 6 m, all drops together at most 78 m, at most 50 devices

garmin-glossary.title: NMEA 2000 Glossary
garmin-glossary.says: a drop cable is at most 6 m, a single backbone cable at most 100 m

actisense-fundamentals.title: 3 fundamentals of designing an NMEA 2000 network
actisense-fundamentals.says: backbone 100 m with lite cable and 250 m with mid or heavy cable, a drop at most 6 m, all drops at most 78 m, at most 50 nodes, one 120 ohm terminator at each end, devices need 9 to 16 V, micro connectors limit the current to 4 A and mini connectors to 8 A

digitalyacht-guide.title: NMEA 2000 Networking Guide
digitalyacht-guide.says: backbone less than 100 m, supply current less than 3 A (60 LEN), 1 LEN is 50 mA, a drop at most 6 m, all drops less than 76 m, at most 50 devices, two terminators

backboneLengthNote: Micro and mini: 100 m (every source). Maxi: 200 m, below the 250 m of the one source that separates heavy cable; Garmin and Digital Yacht give 100 m without naming a cable class. To be reviewed.
totalDropLengthNote: Garmin and Actisense give 78 m, Digital Yacht 76 m. The lower figure is used.
supplyCurrentNote: 3 A (60 LEN). Actisense gives 4 A for micro and 8 A for mini connectors; the lower, class independent figure is used as a warning level above the supply rating you enter.
